LESSON: KENYAN INDIGENOUS GAMES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.11.1: Kenyan Indigenous Games

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Kenyan Indigenous Games. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does water entry skills enhance safety in swimming?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe different ways of water entry in a pool
2. perform a crouch dive into the swimming pool
3. perform backstroke skill in swimming for skill development

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: KENYAN INDIGENOUS GAMES
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Kenyan Indigenous Games helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: KENYAN INDIGENOUS GAMES
Study Kenyan Indigenous Games like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe different ways of water entry in a pool

What this means
In this part you learn to describe different ways of water entry in a pool. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe different ways of water entry in a pool.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Kenyan Indigenous Games” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe different ways of water entry in a pool. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Perform a crouch dive into the swimming pool

What this means
In this part you learn to perform a crouch dive into the swimming pool. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform a crouch dive into the swimming pool.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Kenyan Indigenous Games in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform a crouch dive into the swimming pool. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Perform backstroke skill in swimming for skill development

What this means
In this part you learn to perform backstroke skill in swimming for skill development. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform backstroke skill in swimming for skill development.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform backstroke skill in swimming for skill development. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Kenyan Indigenous Games is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Kenyan Indigenous Games” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe different ways of water entry in a pool)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Kenyan Indigenous Games in your own words. (skill: perform a crouch dive into the swimming pool)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: perform backstroke skill in swimming for skill development)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Kenyan Indigenous Games to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe different ways of water entry in a pool.
3. Practise this skill: perform a crouch dive into the swimming pool.
4. Practise this skill: perform backstroke skill in swimming for skill development.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Kenyan Indigenous Games from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Kenyan Indigenous Games: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Kenyan Indigenous Games?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does water entry skills enhance safety in swimming?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Kenyan Indigenous Games means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe different ways of water entry in a pool.
5. Be able to: perform a crouch dive into the swimming pool.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
